text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer Logitech makes the best universal remote controls and they keep introducing new models that are better and better. If you have half a dozen (or more) remote controls on your living room table and are always losing some of them or forgetting which does what, then a universal remote is for you.

The Harmony 950 appears to be mostly the same as the Harmony Elite, except without the Harmony Hub device. The Harmony Hub can be purchased separately later, though the Elite package is cheaper if you're getting it anyway. The Harmony Hub greatly expands the range and capabilities of your Harmony remote, so you should think twice before skipping it.

Logitech also sells much cheaper Harmony remotes without the touch screen. The main benefit of the touch screen is to program shortcuts to your favorite TV channels and to control more devices than the non-touch remote controls can access. If you always use your DVR or cable box's on-screen channel menu and only have a few devices, then maybe a much cheaper Harmony without the touch screen is a better value for you.

The Harmony is pretty easy to program by connecting to your PC and connecting to the Logitech website. If you have an older Harmony remote, you may be able to transfer all your device settings to this one. The buttons on the Harmony are easy to see, well spaced and give you good feedback when pressed.

Battery life is OK for a touchscreen device, but like your smartphone you will need to recharge this at least every couple of days. Most people will leave the Harmony in the recharging station most of the time, so make sure you have an electrical outlet close to where you will be using the Harmony.

If you're in the market for a universal remote, Logitech Harmony should be first on your list. The only decision you have to make is which model to buy. If you're trying to control a handful of devices (TV, cable box, DVR, stereo system, game system, DVD player), then you really have to ask yourself if the touchscreen feature is worth the big price premium. If you have a "smart home" with remote controlled lights, outlets, thermostat, etc or if your devices are spread around a large room so the IR remote has trouble connecting with them, then the Harmony Hub is a good idea.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer

ELECOM Relacon Handheld Trackball Mouse, Thumb Control, 2.4GHz Wireless, Ergonomic Design, 10-Button Function with Smooth Tracking, Windows11, MacOS (M-RT1DRBK) I've bought and currently use both variants of the Relacon mouse. I'm putting this review on the wireless version.

Overall, 5 stars for the wireless with dongle, 3 stars for the Bluetooth. Unfortunately the Bluetooth one is a bit choppy with tracking, causing the pointer to jump to a random place on the screen often enough to be annoying. The dongle one doesn't have this issue for me. Otherwise they're identical in function and feel.

As a dedicated thumb trackball user since the early 90s, I love it! It is much better quality than any other ambidextrous thumb trackball I've optimistically tried over the years when looking for an alternative to the standard right (or rare left) dedicated handed thumb trackball. I have never been able to get comfortable or quick with finger trackballs, no matter how much I have wanted to or worked at it. Same with the Thinkpad trackpoint.

It is a physical relief to have a mouse that I can use in a neutral wrist position without having my hand or arm stretched out. It is especially nice to be able to transfer and use the mouse with my left hand when I need to type or do something else with my right.

I haven't installed the software or tried to remap the buttons. I just plug in the dongle or pair with Bluetooth, and Windows recognizes it. Since my displays are 1080 or smaller, I keep the speed or acceleration or dpi setting at 1 blink. The button is below the power switch, so I do accidentally tap it occasionally, but it's quick and easy to cycle back to 1.

The stand is more stylish than functional, and even with practice the mouse will sometimes slide right off, but at least it's included. Most of the time, I just switch it off and set the mouse on its side.
text_fidelity_b: ELECOM Relacon Handheld Trackball Mouse, Thumb Control, 2.4GHz Wireless, Ergonomic Design, 10-Button Function with Smooth Tracking, Windows11, MacOS (M-RT1DRBK)

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation I have some cognitive impairment and mobility challenges from lupus, and I was able to set up Fire TV really easily. The batteries go in the remote; the hdmi cable goes where it goes, and the power plugs in where it plugs in. The interface is simple and intuitive, and you can get everywhere with the home button, the directionals, back, and select. The only painful part for me/my hands was logging into my wireless network via the onscreen qwerty keyboard.

The screens are responsive with virtually no latency, thanks to the quad core processor and 2 gb ram. And video streaming is also very smooth. I have only been using this a day, but I haven't had it pause to buffer yet. I have a Chromecast in my son's room, a recent model Mac Mini in the living room, an older C2D Mac Mini in my room with Boxee on it, and a Raspberry Pi, and they all buffer at some point during just about every movie. I stayed in a vacation home with a Roku 2 last summer, and it was great, but it also had to buffer a lot. We also have three game consoles that have streaming video apps, and they buffer, too. I think the Fire's secret may be its wifi card. I am sure that, at some point, my ISP will find a way to slow it down.

So, yeah, I am giving the Fire TV four stars for doing exactly what I need it to do. I had come to Amazon to get another Chromecast, but I saw this and thought it would probably be better suited to what I need in my bedroom (I need my husband to be able to watch a tv show without my help - he is completely tech-challenged and cannot work the Dish remote - too many buttons).

The reason it doesn't get five stars is that there aren't yet enough content apps. There is a manga channel, a documentary channel, an art house channel, along with Crackle and Flixter and Plex (Plex is a for pay service that lets you stream your home content). There is plenty to watch if you are a Prime member (I am - and I appreciated having that already set up on my Fire TV - Thank you, Amazon!) I am also a Dish subscriber, with HBO and a Hopper. I have apps for those directly on some of my devices. I can get them on the internet on the tbs I have hooked up to computers. I can even blast them over to my Chromecast from my tablets. But they aren't on Fire TV, and none of my tablets will screencast to Fire TV. Soon as they are, this is a five star device for me.

I read in Entertainment Weekly that HBO and Amazon Prime have come to an understanding that will make lots and lots of HBO shows available through prime, which will also make them available through Fire TV. For the ones that are not, HBOGO will have an app for this. Between that news and my son's enjoyment of an eight dollar (as opposed to 40 to 60 dollars) platformed on this thing, I am adding a star.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I first became enamored of the garmin company after using the one with a rental car. The ease of use and accuracy was impressive. Unfortunately, that model is no longer in production so I opted for this unit.

In general I am pleased. Easy to set up, the unit features a bright, clear screen. It is a snap to use and the directions have been unfailing accurate. I drive alot and so far have used this unit throughout New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, DC and Virginia. I have had no problem with reception even while traversing mountainous regions. I appreciate the advance notice for turns and the voice command system is a convenience.

However, this unit is not flawless. The robotic voice often mispronounces street names and the voice command system seems a bit hard of hearing when it comes to addresses. I have had to pull over and type in the address. The unit does not like to deviate from its chosen route. For instance, one location I frequent in New York is accessible both by the thruway (toll road) and other non-toll main arteries. Both are about the same distance. When I want to avoid the toll route, the unit will recalculate directing that I turn around and follow the initial route multiple times before adjusting to the alternate route. A big deal, no,but annoying nonetheless. While I have not been terribly plagued by the pop ups, they are annoying and potentially unsafe. While the start up guide and manual are adequate, they are barely so. Whatever happened to detailed instructions? But my biggest gripe is the customer service. I called twice with questions and had ridicualously long waits of fifteen minutes and twenty-five minutes respectively. There is no round the clock service. The last time I called it wasnt even available all week, totally unacceptable.

So while I like this system,there is room for improvement.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

That's an issue of aesthetics, not function. I'd be worried about sitting it on the edge of the tub, as it is too likely to fall.

The one trick to remember, when sticking the antenna to the shower wall, is that suction cups don't work as well on a wet surface. Thoroughly dry the wall first, then place it. It helps will the issue of the antenna falling.

This review is long overdue. I bought these because I was having a problem with a neighbor trespassing on my Mountain property. We had put up numerous game cameras to catch him in the act sadly this unscrupulous character stole those game cameras.

Frustrated as we felt the local sheriff wouldn’t do anything unless we actually caught him red-handed, I bought cheap game cameras and gutted them. I bought four of these devices and installed them behind the battery cover for these now gutted game cameras.

We make sure to put 2 of them up when he was outside and watching. Seven hours later I was sitting on the sofa and evening and I got an alert that one of the trackers started moving. I couldn’t believe this was correct and grabbed my wife while I kept refreshing the tracker all the while taking screen grabs from my phone. We called the sheriff department and they came out and were amazed at the specificity of where the tracker had been.

While I was talking to the deputies in my driveway we heard the neighbor start up his ATV and I made a comment that he’s up to no good.

When we looked at the final data at the moment The neighbor started his ATV one of the trackers all of a sudden went from zero and 1 mph to 6 mph. And then one the trackers stopped moving and was showing back on my property. Another tracker was still showing on the neighbors property and the deputies were able to go right to the spot I showed them on the map in the app and get it.

Clearly, he realized something was up with all the sheriff deputies driving by and tried to get rid of the evidence.

The deputies asked me to send them the times and locations for their report and I said I’ll do you better and exported it all to an excel spreadsheet that had hyperlinks to where the tracker was at anytime. It also included the GPS lat/long. You can totally customize the report you want to see down to the exact hour!

My neighbor was cited for trespassing, theft and criminal mischief.

I also called the company and spoke with Stephen as the one tracker that got thrown back into my property had a cracked battery door. They freely mailed me out a replacement cover. Great product backed up with fantastic customer service.

I pay the month to month plan of $20/tracker and am totally satisfied. Don’t even complain about the monthly, because if something is valuable enough for you to need to track it, then $20 bucks a month is nothing.

And BTW, this thing is tiny!

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link Deco Mesh WiFi System(Deco M5) –Up to 5,500 sq. ft. Whole Home Coverage and 100+ Devices,WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Anitivirus, 3-pack This review is for the TP-LInk Mesh WiFi M5 system.
—————
Amended April 28, 2020
Now that I’ve been using this for a couple weeks, I am returning to add these units HAVE NOT cured the dead spots that needed more signal strength. Yes, the WiFi signal is present in those areas of my home. However, the signal strength has not improved over what my centrally located router produced on its own. Essentially for my roughly $125, I got a couple stylish WiFi access points. What I DID NOT GET is the improved coverage promoted in the description.
—————
This IS NOT a plug it in and it works system. You need to know at minimum:
—Your current router’s IP address, the user ID for it, and the password. If you haven’t changed them from the default, you have no business installing a network anything, because you put EVERYTHING on your system at high risk for hacking. Why? The problem is that the default user ID and password are the SAME FOR ALL routers of the same brand (every brand router has a published default user id and password).
—You need to know which of several comm protocols your ISP uses.
—You need to know that IF YOU SWAP OUT YOUR ROUTER for one of the units, the others WILL NOT WORK to extend your WiFi network. For that you need to set these up as extenders, with the first being connected to your existing router.
—To set up a network of WiFi extenders, you need to know how to turn your existing router’s WiFi transmission off. Only then can you use these as extenders, satellites, or whatever you know them as.
—You are highly likely to have to update the firmware on each M5 device.
—You should set aside about two to three hours to set up a network of multiple devices.
—If you set these up as extenders, some of the default security features are switched off. You need to be sure these security features are enabled on your router instead.

I found this an unacceptably under-documented product that forces you to comb through the internet for proper setup tips. I loathe their little booklet that is “documentation” since it is a collection of single pages in multiple languages that direct you to the App Store or Google Play for the app that manages setup. That app is underpowered, has little relevant or helpful information.

I’ve been working with and installing systems from early (1990s) mainframes, Apple IIs, Macs, PCs of all flavors, and networks right up to now. Were it not for that experience, I might never have gotten this to work. Once installed, it works fine.

Recommendation: If your current router is older, you’re probably more likely to get better WiFi coverage by purchasing a newer, more current router. Try that first, and if you don't get the coverage you need, add a couple or three of these.

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS Transformer Book T100HA-C4-GR 10.1-Inch 2 in 1 Touchscreen Laptop (Cherry Trail Quad-Core Z8500 Processor, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, Windows 10), Gray This is a tablet running a real operating system (Windows 10) hooked up to a small keyboard with a trackpad. And it's all right.

It's thicker and heavier but smaller than my 11 inch MacBook Air, which makes it more convenient in some respects and less convenient in others. The MacBook Air is a used 2012 model with a Core i5 and 4gb ram. It's snappy, but it didn't come with an SD slot, and used it cost about a hundred more than this. The quad core atom processor on the transformer book is pretty fast for a tablet, but it is definitely a lightweight compared to a core i5. Or even an i3.

My iPad Air runs iOS. Way less versatile than Windows 10 in terms of doing work-a-day things, having a browser respond the way you're used to having it respond, etc., but it's still pretty good. However, the keyboard experience is something of a pain, especially since there's no trackpad and you have to touch the tablet face to do the mouse-like things. And using the mail program is harder on the iPad than it is on a mac laptop or on the transformer book.

The transformer book is noticeably slower than either of the other devices, but I was able to do everything I set out to do on it. The Office apps are good and integrate seamlessly with the other Office installations on my other stuff. The screen is as nice as or nicer than my iPad Air. I had a MeMo for a year, and I loved the screen on that. This is very similar - excellent resolution, nice and bright, a bit wider aspect than what the iPad Air has.

The sound is about as good as one would expect. Which is to say, meh. But that's what headphones are for.

Cortano makes it easy to get set up. I asked it to find the apps I wanted. When I want something from the control panel, I ask for that. Since this is my first time with Windows 10, having the assistant helps a lot.

There do seem to be some battery issues. Charging takes a long time. There was an issue with the MeMos, as well, that I sort of resolved by fully cycling the battery a couple of times.

All things considered, I like this tablet/transformer book quite a bit. My only significant issue with it is weight. For my purposes, the ultralight notebook or the regular tablet will meet my needs on any given day. However, if you like your PC desktop and need, essentially, a shuttle craft, though. this is a pretty good compromise machine. It's a decent enough tablet. You can do business stuff, check email, surf the web, and watch movies. You won't be transcoding video or playing resource intense games, but this ultimately is a nice tablet with a keyboard. Not a desktop substitute. Maybe not even a laptop substitute, depending on your needs. But definitely a nice tablet.

UPDATE WITH USAGE ISSUES:

I was getting really annoyed with battery life/charging issues. My iPad Air will stand by for a couple of weeks, no problem, whereas this thing dies if I leave it off the charger a couple of days. It also needs its OEM charger if you intend to charge it within a few hours time, as opposed to overnight and then some. I was able to solve some of this by running task manager and disabling some of the high impact background apps (Microsoft OneDrive is a big offender). And, similar to my other Asus tablet, the battery charging problem seems to improve with conditioning. On the positive side, the more I use this, the better I like it.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS Transformer Book T100HA-C4-GR 10.1-Inch 2 in 1 Touchscreen Laptop (Cherry Trail Quad-Core Z8500 Processor, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, Windows 10), Gray

Seiki SE401GS 40-Inch 1080p 120Hz Slim LED HDTV This led tv is much better than I expected it to be for the price I paid for it. I was not in the market for a new television, but the one I had in my bedroom died. It's a small room, and the dead tv was 26 inches. I started looking for something around that size and stumbled on this one for not too much more than a smaller one. So, I figured I'd give it a try, and if I liked it, I'd put the 32 inch tv from my living room in the bedroom.

Set up was very easy. I put it together using the stand. I had enough screws. They all fit. You have to screw them all the way in straight, or the tv kind of wobbles on the stand, but once I did that, the thing is very stable.

It has one component input, one composite, one antenna, one VGA, and three hdmi, and I'm using all of them. Very very easy. the whole thing, including moving the other tv, took half an hour, with the only slight pain being that my late 2010 Mac Mini won't under scan at 1080p, so I had to go to 720p, on the hdmi connection. I don't even know what any of that means, except that this is what I had to do in order to be able to see my menu bar.

Picture is really nice for the price, even my little intel atom its box over the VGA looks good. What impressed me most is the sound. I only use the tv's speakers for the Wii U, and they are surprisingly clear. I'm still figuring out some of the settings, but up and running in half an hour and enjoying the results is pretty amazing - especially for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Seiki SE401GS 40-Inch 1080p 120Hz Slim LED HDTV

Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000 Though I have a laptop, I decided to use this solid-state drive as a boot drive on my desktop computer. If you are unfamiliar with the difference between a solid-state and a regular hard drive, the solid-state has no moving parts, which makes it silent, fast, reliable, and shock resistant. It has twice the capacity and twice the speed of the solid-state drive I got a couple of years ago for the same price, and blows away a standard drive for speed.

Given the silence and speed, it makes a great boot drive for running Windows, Photoshop, and other programs where speed is a huge advantage. Just to give you an idea, when upgrading from a regular two-year-old hard drive to this solid-state drive, my Windows boot time went from two minutes to about 10 seconds. Seriously, my computer now starts up and is ready to use in like 10 seconds.

What I do is use a solid-state drive as my boot drive and a regular hard drive as a storage drive. Solid-state drives like this are really expensive to purchase if you need any kind of capacity, but a 200 GB drive will certainly hold all of your programs and often used files.

As for this drive specifically, I hooked it up to my desktop and it was immediately recognized by Windows. The drivers installed automatically. In order to make the drive show up as a drive and work in Windows 7, I had to right-click on computer, click manage, double-click storage, double-click disk management, partition it, give it a drive letter, and format it.

As I said, it's a lot faster than the solid-state drive I had from a couple years ago, and there's no problem using it on my desktop machine rather than my laptop.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000

Pros

text_fidelity_a:
Ultimate Ears MEGABOOM 3 Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (Powerful Sound + Thundering Bass, Bluetooth, Magic Button, Waterproof, Battery 20 hours) - Lagoon Blue I used to be a big Ultimate Ears guy from the aughts before they were bought by Logitech who killed their best product lines and replaced it with stuff like... THIS. The tiresome photos of impossibly gleeful adult-babies listening to music underwater and having the times of their lives thanks to this f——g speaker really gets cloying when it’s printed on literally everything except the device itself. But that’s Logitech for you. Of all things I have to complain about with this speaker, the sound isn’t one of them. Unlike its predecessors and smaller cousins, the Megaboom 3 doesn’t peak out the bass quite so much when it would otherwise be distorted. (This is the most common bit of digital audio gimmickry to fool you into think it sounds “crystal clear”.) The people complaining about this speaker in these reviews who say other brands are better are just brands more notorious for “loudness fakery” to make the sound seem more bass-heavy but is really just slick audio post-processing. It’s makes hip hop sound a little better but everything else is a murky mess. But I digress. This speaker does all of the digital trickery, sure, but at least the actual amplifier and speaker drivers aren’t rubbish so that’s I plus. I was playing System of a Down cranked in my bedroom and it sounded amazing, especially compared to my former Boom speaker which someone nicked from my garage. Where the Boo crumpled trying to product screeching highs and thumping lows the Megaboom 3 dominated. Of course I don’t use any of the EQ tomfoolery and let it play as close to how the music was engineered to play and its just dandy. Okay then, good sound: check.
The problem with this speaker, like all of the other UE speakers, is the brain-dead user interface and obnoxious audio feedback that you can’t properly adjust without hacking the device configs (allegedly). There is literally a single on/off switch for all audio feedback. Wut? No relative volume of system sounds compared to music, or selection of which sounds you want to hear and which ones you don’t, like that HORRIBLY OBNOXIOUS LOUD BEEP it makes that’s louder than the music if you accidentally lean in on your volume up button? Of course every sound is as loud as or louder than the music your playing. That’s just great. Furthermore, if you are listening to music through your iPad or iPhone, it decides to insert little beeps for certain feedback notifications that never happen when you are just using your device without the speaker. It’s horribly distracting and unnecessary, but worse is that you NEED audio feedback on if you want to be able to Bluetooth connect to it as audio feedback is the only feedback you get.

Ugh. Sorry, had a bit of a rant there.

It’s tough because I think the speak sounds decent and almost worth the price, but the UI team at Logite... excuse me... Ultimate Ears are clearly huffing paint fumes as each product they subsequently release is even more unpleasant to use than the last. Don’t let the coked-out looking teens with bright, expensive clothing printed on the box fool you.
text_fidelity_b: Ultimate Ears MEGABOOM 3 Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (Powerful Sound + Thundering Bass, Bluetooth, Magic Button, Waterproof, Battery 20 hours) - Lagoon Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Maxell Full Size Illuminated Keyboard CkI-1 This keyboard works pretty well. Good amount of resistance in the keys, and it has lasted me almost two years. It is just now starting to lose accuracy in one of the shift buttons.

Pros: Has lasted fairly well. Keys are lit enough to make viewing easier without being too bright. Convenient hot keys. VERY convenient mute key is the top right corner where it is easy to find quickly. A little "clacky" but not super noisy. Few accidental letter presses. Build quality is pretty good.

Cons: The enter key is according to a non-US layout. The \ button is right beside the enter, and it took me about a year to stop accidentally typing a slash. If you are used to this layout it is fine, but do be aware that it is not the standard US keyboard layout.

Other: the volume knob is very handy, though after a year and a half it mysteriously fell off... not sure if it was misused by my kids or if it was spontaneous.

Bottom line: it's a good build and it should work for you if you prefer this (international?) keyboard layout over the standard US keyboard layout.
text_fidelity_b: Maxell Full Size Illuminated Keyboard CkI-1

Kindle Lighted Leather Cover, Burgundy Red (Fits Kindle Keyboard) I don't know if I'd have bought this for myself sight unseen because I'm pretty much a cheapskate unless I know that spending more actually means better quality. I don't buy things just for the labels.

My husband bought me a Kindle and this cover for Christmas and I am in love with both. The case is obviously well made throughout. The leather and binding are solid. The material on the inside covers is lovely to the touch and, not being slick, it offers a little resistance to slipping if you are resting it on another cloth-covered surface like an overstuffed chair arm.

I often read in bed in the dark and love the way the cover works here. At some angles there's a bit of a flare of light on the screen closest to the light, but a little adjustment fixes that. It's tens times easier than wrestling with a paperbound book and an attached book light.

I find that I take my Kindle out of the cover fairly often to play games or do anything much with the key pad. The first day or so I scared myself by not lining it up quite properly and having the top hinge engaged while the bottom one was only part of the way hooked in. I just patiently and gently worked it till the top hinge disengaged and made a mental note to pay a little attention when I slip the Kindle onto the hinges.

Great product.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Lighted Leather Cover, Burgundy Red (Fits Kindle Keyboard)

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell (1st Gen) – 720p HD video, motion activated alerts, easy installation – Satin Nickel I'm an early adopter of lots of "smart everything" internet connected products (Nest stuff, Smart Grill, SmartVents, internet connected cars, etc.). I have found the Ring doorbell to be one of the most useful and reliable of these types of products. Remote functions that are really valuable to me:
* Remotely "greet" and reschedule the delivery guy who was 2 hours late, while you are out doing other other errands. Warning - it does really freak out most delivery guys to hear your voice emanating from the doorbell button !
* Receive confirmation that your tween/teen has made it home from school, even when they don't see fit to call or text. Plus do a body count to see if any "extras" are visiting. Plus also have a concrete, time-stamped log of any late night returns, so you don't have to stay up late to intercept returning teens.
* Capture video evidence of stolen packages, unwanted solicitations, and prowlers.
The cloud recording cost of 30$/yr is a far better value than other services like Next or Flir. Ring is the clear choice for door monitoring as well as a really cool doorbell.

My only caveats for buyers:
* Take care with the physical installation on very rough surfaces like rough stucco. Holes need to exactly align (no slotted mounting holes) plus the mount plate is sensitive to bending. If the most bends too much to conform to the wall, the actual button/bell unit will not attach.
* Make sure your WiFi signal is strong enough in the location where you are planning install the ring. Plaster and stucco (with embedded screening) attenuate WiFi signals. WiFi basestation with beam-forming really do help (one of my neighbors needed to swap an Apple Airport Express for an Airport Extreme Basestation to achieve reliable and no-laggy video, but now the Ring works like a charm)
* Make sure your transformer is putting out an in-spec voltage, for a wired installation. Mine worked fine, but the another neighbor who recommended the Ring to me wen through two units (replaced by Ring), before they determined the doorbell voltage from the transformer was too high. Things worked flawlessly with the third unit when my neighbor moved to unwired operation.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell (1st Gen) – 720p HD video, motion activated alerts, easy installation – Satin Nickel

text_fidelity_a:
TV Antenna - 1byone Amplified 50 Mile HDTV Digital Antenna Powerful Amplifier Signal Booster for All TV 4K UHF VHF 1080P Local Channels with 20ft Coaxial Cable This is a review of the 50 mile OUS00-0562 model. To summarize: It works. But it's no better than my cheap [[ASIN:B000HKGK8Y RCA Indoor FM and HDTV Antenna]] antenna that I was trying to replace, yet costing several times more.

With my cheap RCA "rabbit ears" antenna I was getting 18 channels, being 8 miles away from the transmitter. According to my digital-to-analog converter most TV signals were in the range of 75% to 30%. I was looking for a better antenna to improve the signal quality, so when I saw that the OUS00-0562 model was on sale I bought it. I didn't believe the 50 mile claim of this antenna since most antennas with this claim are large, more expensive and rather directional. But I figured that even if it was half that it had to be better than my RCA one. Whatever this antenna was directional of not was not specified, I assumed that it was not.

The OUS00-0562 model comes with an antenna with a 20 foot non-removable cord. This was disappointing, but I should have realized this when looking at the product pictures. Having so much cable slack is a waste when it sits 3 feet from the TV. Before I installed the 1byone antenna I took note of signal strength of each channel of my RCA antenna. The OUS00-0562 package also comes with an amplifier, which I connected to my RCA antenna as a test - and was disappointed. Only 3 channels were 10% higher, and that was within margin of error. The OUS00-0562 disappointed me soon after, as there was no change in signal strength on any channel over the RCA antenna (except that it gave me two more channels at 40% signal).

The short version:

RCA "rabbit ears" - 18 channels, 75%-30% (+/- 5%)
RCA "rabbit ears" with 1byone amplifier - 18 channels, 70%-30% (+/- 5%)
1byone OUS00-0562 with 1byone amplifier - 20 channels, 70%-30% (+/- 5%)

I tried to reposition the OUS00-0562 antenna to see if there was a directional issue, if I was out of the "sweat spot." I did notice 5-10% dips here and there but no marked improvements. I didn't spend much time on this and since it wasn't shipped with a stand. You can buy one, but I didn't want to spend any more money on it since to me it was overpriced as is. I promptly returned it.

I will give this antenna one point though. It's better looking than the RCA antenna and it takes up less space. So if looks and space matter, it might be for you.
text_fidelity_b: TV Antenna - 1byone Amplified 50 Mile HDTV Digital Antenna Powerful Amplifier Signal Booster for All TV 4K UHF VHF 1080P Local Channels with 20ft Coaxial Cable

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging I have a Nuvi 360. It came with a suction cup windshield mount. It also came with a steel disk with double sticky adhesive on the back. I was supposed to mount this disk somewhere on my dashboard, then use the suction cup to attach the mount. I didn't want to use the suction mount directly onto the windshield because 1) it telegraphs the presence of an expensive GPS unit, 2) it's illegal in California to attach anything to the windshield and 3) I don't think the suction cup would last very long.

Then there's the disk with the very permanent double sticky tape. The problem with almost all cars these days is there really isn't anywhere to attach the disk discreetly. Every square inch is taken with existing stuff. And who wants an ugly disk glued to the dash anyway? And what if I want to use the GPS in other vehicles? More disks?

So I settled on this "beanbag" mount with the ball mount arm.

Unfortunately, before the beanbag friction mount arrived, I was flexing the arm in the suction cup mount and noticed the suction cup's mounting bracket had already broken. I had never even attached it to anything! The mount is beautifully engineered and built...except for one area where the arm's hinge pin attaches to the suction cup's plastic hinge loops. The loops are too thin and fragile. The loops cracked and broke with hardly any hinging at all.

So now I have a quite useless suction mount but a very functional ball arm. What to do?

I drove the hinge pin out of the ball arm. Then I took two small 1" x 1" steel angle brackets and attached them to the ball arm with a 2" long, 8-32 threaded machine screw and an 8-32 wingnut. This created two "feet" for the ball arm. Then I epoxied the two bracket "feet" to the fabric (upper) side of an old 1/4" thick mousepad. Ta da. A friction pad for pennies with a ball arm attached.

Works great. Cost was virtually nothing. Doesn't slide on either of the two dashboards I've tried it on. The mousepad is flexible and conforms easily to the curving shape of the various dashboards. It doesn't weigh much but the thick mousepad has enough heft to plant the getup nicely. The grippy rubber side of the mousepad adheres nicely to the dash. Yet I can pull it down to the floor quickly and reposition it easily.

I wish I'd thought of this BEFORE I ordered this "official" friction mount to the tune of a couple of twenties.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging

text_fidelity_a:
SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V Here are my thoughts about Roku. Generally I like the product, but in setting it up I had some concerns.

PROS:
**Easy to set up
**Compact - it's so small it fits in one hand.
**Picture quality is pretty sharp depending upon the source. It is not HD quality but more like a decent DVD (though not Blu-Ray).
**A number of free channels available through Roku. You can add a lot of content. Since I'm an old movie buff, I added Pub a Hub (public domain movies) and Crackle (pretty bad recent movies but some good classics, like Easy Rider).
**Picture is big. I have a friend who has a projector that's five times as big as the Roku, and yet the projected image is the same size. That's impressive.

CONS:
**How much radiation does this device emit? In the fine print, the instruction booklet reads: "This equipment complies with FCC radiation exposure limits set forth for an uncontrolled environment. This equipment should be installed and operated with minimum distance 20CM between the RADIATOR AND YOUR BODY."
Hmm. I don't know about you, but it's hard not to sit pretty close to the projector. I used it in the bedroom and watched a movie on the ceiling. Of course I had to be close to it in order to put it at the right angle. How much radiation is the device emitting?

**Roku asks for your credit card information before you can use the device. When you set up an account, even if you don't want anything other than the free channels, they force you to put your credit card on file. The other privacy issue I object to is the way Roku allows you to connect to Facebook. In order for Roku to work, you were pretty much forced to allow Roku to access your information on Facebook at any time (even when you're logged out!) Not happy about this.

**In order to add some channels to the Roku network, you have to establish separate accounts. That means establishing one for Netflix, one for Amazon, etc, if you don't already have one. This means I'm sharing my account information with a number of companies I may or may not want to do business with. No doubt all this information will be shared among the video providers. That means a lot of spam will be coming my way in my email.

**Roku is geared toward convincing you to subscribe to as many streaming (pay on demand) services as possible. I'm not sure I would pay $300 for it, as it is very much a device aimed to getting you to subscribe to streaming channels. You can use it other ways, but Roku feels like a product sponsored by many vendors, as opposed to a stand-alone projector.

My conclusion? I recommend it with some reservations as noted above.

I am hoping to figure out soon how to download WMA audiobook files from my local library onto this device. One of the prime uses I have for an MP3 player like this one is listening to audiobooks when exercising or doing chores around the house.

So far, I am really happy with this new version of a beloved device.

text_fidelity_a:
USB Power Strip Portable Travel Charger Outlets 2.1AMP 1AMP 21W 5Foot Power Supply Cord With Universal Plug Input From 100v-240v Power Sockets USB Charger Station 4 Port 5v 1A/2.1A USB Charger (White) This is a very unique and awesome product. It wasn't listed near the beginning of my Amazon search results, so it took me a while to find it. But it's AWESOME!!!

The first thing I do when I get to a hotel room or a cruise ship cabin is to set up my charging station. We have phones, iWatches, Kindle, iPad, and rechargable power packs, so we end up having a lot of potential things to charge. Setting up the charging area is a high priority. The best place is on a table or desk, so we can spread out our rat's nest of cables and devices with easy access. However, power outlets are often in inconvenient places, especially on a cruise ship. (On cruises, in the past I would actually bring a small extension cord.)

Anyway, this super clever travel charger solves the problem. I can plug it into the wall outlet, and run the cord up onto a table or desk. It's perfect.

Actually, the 4 USB ports isn't nearly enough for us, so one of these chargers wasn't going to entirely solve my problem. Theoretically, I could use two of them, but that's overkill in the sense that I don't need long two cords. Since this charger has a wall-plug type of outlet on the charger itself, I already have regular wall power at the charger on the table. I don't need to run a second cord from a wall outlet. Therefore, I use a small 4-port USB charger without the cord, and plug that into this charger. That gives me 8 USB ports up on the table for easy access. Here's the 4-port charger without a cord that I plug into this one:
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07JH9R89T/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o01_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

I have never seen a charger with a cord like this before, and I am very impressed with how clever and useful the design is! The one problem I found was with the child protection piece inside the slots on the charger's power socket. (This is the 110V power socket on the charger.) Because of the child protection piece, it can sometimes be very hard to get something plugged into that socket. The protection piece needs to slide to the side, so you can't just push the plug straight in, like you would at a wall socket. You need to put the prongs into the slots at an angle, and pry the protection piece out of the way. It's a pain. So, if you don't need the child protection, and you intend to use that socket, you'll probably want to remove the protection piece.

Here's how to do that. The top surface is a snap-off cover. Pull it up in the middle of one of the side, and slip a little screwdriver in there to carefully pry around and pop it off. Then there's a second cover inside that isn't attached, and will almost just fall out. On the back of that second cover, you'll see the two little springs and the plastic protection piece. Pull out the springs and the protection piece, and then put it all back together.

[NOTE: Do not remove the child protection if there will be children near it, or if you have any other safety concerns about its removal. Remove it at your own discretion and your own risk. I'm not telling you to remove it. I'm just telling you how to remove it if you want to.]

Anyway, I actually went a step further. The socket seems to be designed to accept any plug in the universe, so there are a lot of extra holes and spaces (i.e. it's not just two little slits for the normal US plug). I took white electrical tape, and taped over all the extra holes and spaces on the secondary (internal) cover, leaving just the two slits open. Then after popping on the outer cover, you just see the two open slits. All the other openings are covered internally with the white electrical tape. I think it looks much better, but this is purely a cosmetic step.

At first, it seemed like the clip for the plug is on the wrong side. It's on the same side as the USB ports. If you leave the plug in the clip (and leave the cord wrapped around the charger), then rotate the plug down 90 degrees, you can plug it into a wall outlet and the charger would be flush against the wall, hanging down from the wall socket. That seemed like it should be a nice neat way of using it without extending the cord, if desired. However, you can't do that because the USB ports end up against the wall, and you can't access them. If the clip was on the opposite side, it would work fine. As it currently is, in order to use it, you need to flip it around so the USB ports are facing out. But since the plug clip is on the wrong side, the charger sticks out from the wall at an angle. At first this seemed like a design flaw. Then I read in the instructions where it specifically says you shouldn't do any charging while the cord is wrapped around it. Presumably that's a heat issue. Therefore, it is probably designed this way on purpose, to discourage you from attempting to use the charger with the cord wrapped around it.

The bottom line is that there is no design flaw. It's prefect just the way it is. And you need to unwrap the cord when you use it, which is fine with me, since having the cord extended is the best feature of this charger.

Anyway, I think this is an awesome little gadget.
text_fidelity_b: USB Power Strip Portable Travel Charger Outlets 2.1AMP 1AMP 21W 5Foot Power Supply Cord With Universal Plug Input From 100v-240v Power Sockets USB Charger Station 4 Port 5v 1A/2.1A USB Charger (White)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer So far this is my initial view of this remote just having downloaded the software and set up the initial action. Logitech, you guys need to have your heads examined. It's a REMOTE. I should not need a computer in the first place to set up a REMOTE. To add insult to this injury, they claim since I have macOS Catalina that their 32-bit software will not work. Ah, hello McFly? 32-bit apps?? Seriously? The 20th century called, they want their tech back. We've been using 64 bit for at least a decade. It is 2020 now. You know... Unbelievable. If you can't write software, fold it all up and go home. You don't deserve our money.

First mistake by Logitech. Ultimately, there IS a 64-bit app. So why do you still have a message on your web site saying we'll need an update? Here's a tip for you guys. YOU CAN JUST SUPPLY the 64-bit app right there on that screen. You could easily say for Catalina and above, click here, else get the older, lamer, 32-bit version. I have to click on a link, which seems to tell me you don't have it, which goes in a bit of a circle, before ultimately telling me that you do in fact have it.

Next, the 950 has this super stiff cover for the Micro USB connector, also technology from the cretaceous period. I think we found one of these cables in the mouth of Coleophysis bauri remains from 250 million years ago. I wasn't sure if I was breaking the thing or pulling off a cap. You software asks if I have a hub for my remote? I bought it, I didn't build it. I have whatever came in the box. Is it a hub, a charging cradle, a spacecraft, an anti-gravity device, a floatation device? I don't know. All I know is I put the device in that thing and your software doesn't detect it. So I proceed to PRY off that cap, hoping it was a cap, and it is. It would be nice if the TINY manual said so.

Before I actually try to use this thing, one more note for you brainiacs at Logitech. It would super if you made the remote with a flat back. I'll give you a guess why I say this. When you make a rounded back, us, meaning your customers, can't leave the remote on a flat surface and press the buttons without it wobbling all over the place. It pretty much becomes a two-handed operation. As luck would have it, I have two hands. But you never know. It would be super if I can just put it on a flat surface and USE it while it sits on the hard surface of, say a coffee table or nightstand.

At this stage, I'd give zero stars if possible. Hopefully the remote can redeem itself in practice. But all this nonsense to get using it in the first place is almost a deal killer. In fact, I'd bet that alone is a deal killer for many.

More to follow.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra SPORT Bluetooth Stereo Headset - Black/Yellow (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I am disappointed with these headphones for only one reason: My ears are small, and because of that, these headphones will not snuggly "hang" over my ears like they should. (Children would have the same problem, I expect.) If the over-ear part of the headphones were a little more moldable, I might be able to make them work for me; the extra ear gels themselves are helpful in getting a good fit into the ear canal, but that doesn't keep them from falling off of me. This is why I'm knocking of a star but, again, the problem is not with the headset but with my own anatomy!

With that caveat aside, I love them! For a gardener who wants to listen to something outside while working, the FM radio works just fine and the yellow rubbery cord keeps them around your neck even if you do knock them off. The U.S. Military-grade protection features (against dust, moisture, and shock) make these headphones stand out from the pack.

The Bluetooth pairing and sustained connection with these is better than any other Bluetooth device I've ever used, although I tend not to use Bluetooth unless I'm up and about in the house doing chores. I also don't make or get a lot of phone calls, so we don't even have a cellphone account and depend on the occasional VoIP to get the job done. Meaning I haven't tested the headset features at all.

But the sound is crisp and clear, without mud, more like monitoring headphones used in the music industry. I feel no pressure when wearing them (holding them to my head with my hands, of course, to keep them from falling off of my teensy ears), and I know they would be very comfortable for me in daily use. Maybe I can come up with something to rig them with so they don't fall off. Because I really do like them.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra SPORT Bluetooth Stereo Headset - Black/Yellow (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I am a big fan of my kindles. I have the kindle keyboard ereaders 1st and 3rd gen , the 2nd gen Fire 8.9" and last year I bought the 6" Fire. I would not have bought this one except that my 6" Fire has gotten glitchy. I have not had problems with any of my kindles before so I chalked it up to just a bad egg.
I was thinking of replacing it when I found this great deal on the lastest 7" Fire. $100 for a tablet is such a deal. $50 is AMAZING!!
There isn't a huge difference other than this one is a little bigger. It was easy to import everything from my old tablet to my new one. My books, photos, songs, even my book marks from Silk. The set up took minutes.
The home page is different, it looks like the ones on iphones with all the apps on the home page. You can group them into smaller collections, you can also upload your own photo to be the wallpaper. I like this better than the carousel. You can also group your books into collections. There is a button so that you can move between applications without them closing out. It will show all the last places you went so you can pick up where you were and just switch screens. This is my favorite new feature, even more than the change with the home screen.
I'm not super fond of Silk but it is less annoying since they did an upgrade.
I have only had one problem: when I was first setting it up, the screen kept freezing. I rebooted it and I haven't had an issue since.
This is just as fast as my 6" tablet. Battery usage seems the same as well. According to the specs this should be a little slower than the 6" with less battery time but I have not noticed a difference. The plastic back feels only a little less durable than my other kindles but I'm not concerned. I feel like I have gotten quite a deal.

text_fidelity_a:
Guardline 500 Foot Range Wireless Driveway Alarm [4 Motion Detector Alarm Sensors & 1 Receiver] Weatherproof Outdoor Security Alert System for Home & Property Update Sep 2022, 5 years later:
One of the few things that has worked great through rain, sleet, snow, heat and all things Mother Nature can throw at it. Been very happy with this purchase! The sensor finally started having issues 5 years later and found the sensor screen cracked and condensation was getting in. Just bought another one! Highly recommend this product!

Update Sep 2018, 1 year later:
It is located out in the weather and everything has worked great through a year of use in our driveway; very cold winter and very hot summer. I changed batteries recently but did so out of precaution, not because the batteries were weak. We drive in and out at least 4-5 times a day, children ride bikes by it many times a week, along with several trips to the mailbox. About the only thing to watch is when replacing batteries the little screws will fall out if not careful so I placed a white towel underneath since our alarm is mounted on a post with pine straw underneath.
Excellent product and has been great, highly recommend. You can see my full review below.

REVIEW:
After researching several products including much cheaper alternatives, I ultimately decided on this particular brand/model. We use this specifically to alert us of cars coming into our driveway. If you are looking to use this for security reasons, be aware the sensor blinks red when motion is detected which can be seen at night.
Based on two week’s usage, I highly recommend this unit thus far and here is my pros, cons, & discoveries after a few weeks of usage:
Pros/Discoveries:
• Easy to setup and install. Read the manual first!
• Transmitter easily mounts to anything. We used a 4”x4” treated post mounted about 3’6” above the ground. Post is overkill but does look nice.
• Does not seem to have many false alarms but will pick up anything within the range of the sensor which has enough movement to trigger the sensor (as it should). Had one alarm over two weeks that we never saw the reason for the alarm. Perhaps something blew across the sensor. We also have a sprinkler system which sprays water across the sensor and it never alerts, which is good.
• Install the sensor at least 3-4’ above the ground which will avoid most dogs/cats/squirrels, etc., and do not place it on metal. I also would not place it near/within range of bushes/tree limbs or similar items which might move with the wind.
• Adjust the sensitivity distance on the sensor (you must remove the four screws on the sensor to do this). Our driveway is for one car so I decreased the sensitivity level to 23’ (set 39’ from the factory). Options are 13’, 23’, 26’ and 39’.
• You can easily adjust the angle of the sensor once installed.
• Has a sensor low battery indicator which flashes inside on the receiver.
• Easy to add other sensors if needed up to 16 (4 on each zone).
• Uses common batteries. Sensor takes four AA batteries (should last a year); receiver uses four AAA batteries and/or wall outlet power. Receiver can be plugged in with batteries installed acting as a battery backup if power is lost.
• Receiver has plenty of sound melodies to select (~30), and can be very loud if volume is adjusted all the way up.
• No problem with range as our sensor is only about 150’ from the receiver but does go through a couple walls.
• Our sensor is installed in the weather without any other coverings. Based on the instructions it can be mounted anywhere outside and I don’t see the need to put the sensor inside a protective covering.
• I like the removable top of the sensor to keep out weather and sunlight on the sensor.
• The 12 volt relay is a nice option for linking to alarms, gates, or whatever else you might want to do.
• Receiver is easily turned off and on. If leaving home really early on weekends for example, I’ll turn it off to avoid waking my family when I drive out.
• Came with a small screwdriver which fits perfectly to remove tiny screws in the sensor for battery installation and sensitivity setting.

CONS:
• I thought the sensor would have been enclosed in stronger PVC (aka thicker plastic). But it does have a lifetime warranty as long as the company is in business.
• Would have liked more color options for the sensor. For example, black, white and camo.
• Worried about losing the small screws when adjusting sensitivity and/or replacing the batteries in the sensor once installed. Our sensor is installed over a plant bed with pine straw, so I had to put down a white towel under the unit when opening the enclosure to make final sensitivity adjustments. Would have been nice if the sensor came with the type screws that don’t fall out when unscrewed.
• Receiver is not the nicest to look at but we managed to place it where it was centrally located in the house and not so obvious.
• There are over 30 melodies available but we were hoping for more chimes/bells similar to doorbell type options. Many are song type melodies which we didn't like.

Overall very pleased and highly recommend.
I would like to see a wifi enabled version for alerts on a smartphone if desired.
Will update this review should something change.
text_fidelity_b: Guardline 500 Foot Range Wireless Driveway Alarm [4 Motion Detector Alarm Sensors & 1 Receiver] Weatherproof Outdoor Security Alert System for Home & Property

text_fidelity_a:
Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Update: I have now tried two other brands (a coworker's, and bought another brand) of ergonomic mice that both work substantially better than the Anker version, which also cost less! I highly suggest anyone considering buying this, skip over it and look for another one that is cheaper with good reviews. It amazes me that a company with a known name can skip out on quality so much that other product that cost half as much outperform it in every way.

The Good:
Feels great to hold. More natural than a typical mouse. All the buttons are in the right places and do not require any strain to press. The wheel is in the perfect spot to be used by my middle finger, which is typically what I try to do, since I swear I already have arthritis in my point finger being under 30 years old...

The Bad: There is an obvious input delay, making this pretty terrible for anyone who grew up using computers. That no one else has mentioned this is beyond me. Side by side comparison of any of my Logitech mice and this Anker mouse makes the input delay on this mouse even more obvious. It feels like trying to use a mouse on a TV with interpolation (120 Hz, smooth motion, etc.) enabled. On top of the nearly deal-breaking latency issue, the input into the computer is inconsistent, causing the mouse to frequently skip around or miss my movements.

If you expect to play any game that requires any amount of precision or is time-based, you will regret buying this mouse. Games aside, this mouse reduces my productivity because of how unreliable the signal is, and the extra effort needed to predict the movement of the cursor due to the lag.

I tried the wired version of this mouse (a friend had it) and the input lag is not as bad, but is still there. Therefore, I advise against anyone buying this or the wired version, and suggest to instead look elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black

text_fidelity_a:
NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Grey/Green) Although there are a lot of positive points to be said about this product, a major flaw with it is that - even on low volumes and on songs without much bass - you can hear a bit of distortion, like crackly static, that sounds like a speaker that you're either working too hard or is at the end of its life. This becomes worse as the battery gets low. I consider this issue to be "understandable and sort of acceptable" considering the whole system has to run on battery power and most people aren't expecting high power out of such a setup. They might just have a high-pass crossover set too high to conserve power, and too much is cut off, resulting in messy sound.

When you charge your phone with the speaker's battery (which in itself is sort of a nice, if cannibalistic, feature, one that other devices claim even though it is inherent to the device; with this, the USB-A port was added specifically for this purpose), it lowers the volume to level 8 (there is nothing to tell you what level you're at) to keep from draining the battery quickly. Even at this medium level and below, this problem can be recognized.

The bike mounts are 4" apart, center to center, so make sure you have room on your bike handlebars if that is your purpose for ordering. Included bike mounts are good. It also comes with a neoprene case, a USB cable, and an audio cable, both red. With all these extras trying to give the appearance of premium, it doesn't actually come with a charger, not that this will be an issue for most people (you probably already have more than you know what to do with).

There should be keyhole slots built into the bike mounts so it could also be hung on the wall and removed easily, making it more versatile.

The unit pairs easily and immediately with my Blackberry every time, and it can control the tracks through the BT connection as well. It looks well made and has a good feel to it. It looks like it could almost be waterproof, although I noticed no mention or claim of that feature (so I'm sure it's not).

The sound overall isn't bad for a low voltage battery operated speaker, as long as you're not sitting down and listening too closely. I guess for the purposes of making noise as you ride around the neighborhood, it'll do just fine.
text_fidelity_b: NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Grey/Green)

However, I wouldn’t trust this to be your ‘durable case’, say for traveling, commuting, distracting the kids. I am concerned that a fall with this case may cause significant damage, especially as the case ages. I’ve had the case for quite a few months now, and the first thing I can note is that the PVC screen cover is very loose, and needs to be carefully placed when closing it, so that it covers the screen completely. I am no longer able to use the folded screen cover for propping the tablet up anymore, because of the wear.

On a happier note, the case *IS* easy to remove, so you can use a heavier and more protective case when you need to travel. This case adds almost no weight to the tablet as well. The colored part of the PVC hasn’t scraped off or cracked either. So, as a light weight, safe-for-home case, it’s a solid 4. As an ‘all purpose’ case, I’d rate it a 3 on it’s own, or 3.5 if you’re putting it into a computer backpack with a padded chamber for it.

The set-up was so easy that all you had to do was basically turn it on and listen to its instructions on how to pair it, and then all you do is make your calls and go! As someone who doesn't like the Cyborg appearance of the Bluetooth, this one is so tiny it's barely noticeable and I love that it comes with different size ear pads to make sure you are comfortable. The text speak is AMAZING! Who knew technology would come this far and so quickly?!

This device is perfect for techies who have to have the latest and for holdouts like me who can do without it...until they put it on. I love this device! I am a Bluetooth convert!!

Command One is the Air Force One of cellular technology. WHUT!!!!!!!!!

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation Fantastic little box.  I have been a Roku customer for a number of years, but this box takes streaming the internet to another level. I love the content on the Fire Box. I am also a Prime customer, so I feel that I really get to use my membership to the fullest. I love the HBO TV series on Prime also!!! i can watch them for free.  The Roku has 1,000 apps but I find only about 10 that I am interested in. With the Fire Box, I love all the content. Please get an app for DramaFever (Korean TV dramas). My only other criticism is I wish there was a way to separate my gaming apps from the other apps that I installed and used. Currently they are all under the same heading. Other than that, I look forward to the new content that you will be providing for the Fire Box users. I have told a number of my friends about the Fire Box.  They are also Roku owners but I know the content here is more to what they would be looking for. I do not have any cable or satellite service. I strictly use the Fire Box and the Amazon Basic Extreme antenna for all my television needs. With the Basic Extreme antenna, I pick up 23 local channels free.  What I love is the fact that I have better content that what is shown on television and no commercials to boot.  Don't be afraid to dump your expensive cable or satellite service and go with the Fire Box and the Amazon Basic Extreme antenna. You can't go wrong.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation

text_fidelity_a:
HUE Animation Studio: Complete Stop Motion Animation Kit (Camera, Software, Book) for Windows/macOS (Black) Our ten year old grandson has been using a Lego stop action kit for about two years. From what I understood he was becoming unhappy with the quality and positioning capabilities of the camera he was using. The software may have also been a bit clumsy. We decided on the Hue Animation Studio kit (with camera) after surveying many stop-action offerings. Some were quite advanced with features far beyond making stop-action videos, while others appeared to be targeted at a younger child. Few, if any, included a high quality camera. We noticed that the Hue Animation camera alone received excellent reviews. We decided try the whole kit for only $20 more than the camera alone.

Our grandson absolutely loves this kit. The images from the camera a great and it is easy to put into many stable positions. He also likes the software much better than what he had been using before. The build quality of the camera appears to be very good and it should be durable. I think we hit a home run for this ten year old.
text_fidelity_b: HUE Animation Studio: Complete Stop Motion Animation Kit (Camera, Software, Book) for Windows/macOS (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Show - 1st Generation Black I was really surprised by the Show. My first impression was that it's a little bigger than I expected. It's also fairly heavy. Now having used it a few months, I'm glad for the weight. As you are pecking the touch screen with your finger, the extra weight keeps it very stable.

I was anxious to get it started up and see how it's sound compared to my original Echo. I was surprised. I think it sounds better. It has a deeper bass response and the sound is a little more directional with the speakers being in the front.

Other features I really enjoy is that you can load a custom home image, and it constantly scrolls "trending" topics across the home page when not in use. If you see something you want to know more about, you can ask it and it will play the audio or video clip. If you miss something, you can ask it what's trending and it will list everything.

I love that most things you ask it will give the normal Alexa audio response, but also a visual. The weather is a good example. It reads the weather just as an Echo would do, but also shows you the visual on the screen and allows you to scroll through the days ahead with a touch of the finger.

I use it for video calling with a friend who also owns one and it works well. The audio quality is good and we're able to communicate face to face.

I search for and watch youtube videos quite often. If there is something specific you are looking for, it can be painful. The search doesn't always understand slang or complex words, making the search results a little unreliable.

Overall, I really like it. It doesn't "hear" better than the original Echo and does frequently respond when you aren't talking to it, just like the original. It just has a little better sound and a nice touch display screen!
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show - 1st Generation Black

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung 128GB BAR (METAL) USB 3.0 Flash Drive (MUF-128BA/AM) Bulletproof, very large capacity, and FAST if you have USB 3.0 ports to use it with. Backwards compatible. Given a USB 3.0 port, this single drive would be IDEAL for backups, and it's so small you can take it with you rather than worrying about storing an external drive. Beautiful but tough exterior with a big ring for keychains or lanyards. YOU CANNOT HAVE TOO MANY BACKUPS. That's a fact. Set yourself up to look like a genius by having current data on one of these flash drives. USB 3.0 is (theoretically) TEN TIMES as fast as USB 2.0! That's a big deal. Slow drives aren't used as much, people don't want to sit and watch a progress bar crawl along. Samsung is a solid name, I'm much happier trusting a big name than a fly-by-night I've never heard of. Back up your photos and music and business files, then back up the backups. This is a terrific little device, looks great, good and fast. Highly recommended.
---
Surprisingly fast transferring data from a 2.x USB port but it REALLY flies when moving files via a 3.0 USB port!
text_fidelity_b: Samsung 128GB BAR (METAL) USB 3.0 Flash Drive (MUF-128BA/AM)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech MX Revolution Cordless Laser Mouse - Laser - USB I have been using mice since the mid-80s. This is the best mouse I have ever used. It feels very comfortable in my hand and the performance is excellent. Best of all, I go weeks without recharging it. Of course this is my home computer so I don't use it all day every day.

I have used this mouse with both a Dell Latitude laptop (D660?) and a Toshiba T60, both running XP.

I plan on buying a second for use at work.

update - 3/19/2009. I am now using this product with a Lenove T60. It still works like a champ. It seems like it runs forever on a charge. The response/control remain terrific.

update 11/19/2009. OK, there is one problem with charging this mouse. It now doesn't always make great contact in the charging cradle. It seems that it goes too low in the charger to make good contact sometimes. I'm not sure what's going on. I finally figured out a workaround. I lay a piece of string or paper clip in the charging cradle. It holds the mouse up just high enough to make better contact. It's easy to see when it's charging because the 3 LEDs cycle. I still love this mouse, and it seems to go forever on a charge. And, for several months I worked out of a home office exclusively so I really gave it a workout.

OK, I'm on 6.5 years with this mouse now. It does seem like it doesn't hold the charge as long, and I like the new Logitech solution (with the little USB dongle and chargeable with a USB cable) better. I still have not had a mouse perform better. It makes me happy. Maybe I should get out more.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MX Revolution Cordless Laser Mouse - Laser - USB

text_fidelity_a:
Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black) This is a much easier alternative to the My K-cup option if you want to use your own coffee in a K-cup machine rather than the pre-packaged cups. Unlike the My K-cup you don't need to remove the inner cup of the machine to use this. It just drops right in, so you can switch between this and a regular k-cup without having to dismantle anything.

The kit is very complete. There are three cups, each a slightly different color (different shades of brown). The cups are decently made. The plastic sides are nice and thick; the o-ring on the cap is of good quality; and the metal mesh is firmly attached. My only quibble with the build quality is the hinge. It's plastic, and I don't have confidence that it will last a long time before breaking. It's not a big deal, since the cup will still work fine even with a broken hinge, so I'm not docking any points due to that potential problem.

I like that the water dispersion channel has slots all around it to ensure water gets sprayed in all directions inside the cup to keep the grounds uniformly wet. I also really like that the lip area has a slight indent to make it very easy to pop open the top with one hand.

It fit fine in my Cuisinart K-cup machine. The lid of the machine was just slightly raised compared with using a "real" k-cup, but it had zero impact on performance. I tried several different brews, all with good results. You will need to fiddle with the grind level to get the best coffee. Too fine of a grind and it gets over-extracted and bitter; too coarse and it's weak.

Cleaning a used cup is very easy. I pop open the top, hold it upside down in the compost pail, and whack it gently on the base with a wooden spoon. Nearly all the used grounds drop out, and what's left can be easily rinsed under running water. You can also just dump the contents into the disposal or garbage if you don't compost your grounds.

Another option is to use a mini filter in the cup. A package of them are included and, while they do make cleanup easier, I prefer to use just the cup without a filter.

The kit also includes a charcoal filter. I didn't use that, so I can't speak to its performance. It looks to be the same size as the filters used in the water intake of my Cuisinart K-cup machine, so I expect it would perform in a similar fashion.

This Smart Cup kit works well, is well-made/designed, and comes in a very complete kit. Having used the My K-cup version I can confidently say that this performs better and is easier to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black)
